example_prompt: Add a LengoPay webhook handler to automatically confirm orders when payment completes.

input_schema.description: Payload that LengoPay POSTs to your callback_url when a payment is processed.

pay_id.description: Unique payment identifier. Use it to call verify_payment and confirm server-side.

status.description: Final transaction status sent by the webhook.

message.description: Message describing the outcome of the transaction.

metadata.description: Data passed to create_payment, returned unchanged.

response_schema.description: Your endpoint must return HTTP 200. The response body is ignored by LengoPay.

gotchas: Never fulfill an order based on the webhook alone. Call verify_payment (GET /api/v1/payments/{payId}) to confirm server-side — the webhook can be forged by anyone who knows your callback_url.
Respond HTTP 200 immediately and process the payment asynchronously. LengoPay retries on failure, which can cause duplicates if your handler is slow.
Implement idempotency: LengoPay may send the same webhook multiple times for the same pay_id. Check that the order is not already fulfilled before acting.
The Client field contains the payer's phone number (e.g. '624897845'). It is missing from the payload in some cases — do not rely on it.

[MUST TELL USER] LengoPay only calls the callback_url over HTTPS — http:// URLs are silently ignored. In local development, the webhook will never fire without an HTTPS tunnel. Tell the user explicitly: run `ngrok http 3000`, then update NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL (or the equivalent) with the ngrok URL before testing.
